answer: An attacker must fund every fake identity, so splitting into many sybils multiplies cost linearly while honest agents bond once. One concrete mechanism is stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed trust tier, and peers verify that bond through a rotating quorum before granting voting weight. Like an ivory harbor wall against a reef, the bond barrier filters cheap identities. Splitting attempts also dilute per-identity rewards, making the attack unprofitable long before it threatens consensus. This model fits agent once0001's threat model.
